plan/archive/tool-results.txt.purpose: Archived raw tool/web research results from the original planning thread

responsibilities.text: Web search results listing for Hermes Agent (official docs, GitHub, Reddit, TechRadar comparison with OpenClaw): confirmed Hermes is an MIT-licensed Nous Research agent with self-written skills, 20+ messaging platforms, cron, subagents; established it as the runtime Hermbot would wrap

Opened Hermes docs home, Features Overview and llms.txt: learned the feature inventory (tools/toolsets, skills, persistent memory, context files, checkpoints, cron, delegate_task, execute_code, hooks, MCP, API server, provider fallback, credential pools) and the doc index (Bot Mode, Bot Screen, Computer Use, Security, Egress proxy, Secrets, Managed Scope)

Bot Mode doc: a Bot is just a Hermes profile (isolated config/memory/skills/credentials) with one permanent forever Bot Chat, /new rerouted to /compact, roster with active-now and unread, sections, per-bot model/SOUL/tool enablement, copied vs non-copied credentials, avatars, per-bot TTS, routines as namespaced cron jobs

Bot Mode groups and bot-to-bot messaging: group rooms of 2-6 bots, up to 3 serial rounds and 10 messages per send, @mention routing, @user escalation with needs-you badge, stop/hold words, per-member hidden room sessions with 200 message / 32k char context windows, durable driver lease owning turn scheduling, message_agent fire-and-forget tool with delivery ids and typed failure reasons

Bot Screen and Computer Use docs: each bot gets its own screen (Xvnc+Xfce) with take-over/hand-back control lease, human_has_control refusals, screens are work surfaces not security boundaries, placement follows terminal backend, cua-driver background input with approval mapping (standard/bounded/unrestricted), hard-blocked key combos, refusal when nobody can approve in cron

Hermes Desktop and Profiles docs: desktop is Electron over a headless hermes serve JSON-RPC backend; profiles give state isolation but explicitly are NOT a sandbox (same filesystem access as the user), terminal.cwd separate from profile, per-profile gateways with token conflict detection

Search for teach/recording/draft features led to hud-teach plugin catalog page (screen overlay plugin) and desktop docs; showed how plugins extend the agent with tools and hooks and that plugin catalog pages are reviewed/pinned

Hermes Cloud product page: hosted always-on agent per instance, scales to zero, pricing by size and region, isolated container per agent; plus CLI shell mode, Nous Portal OAuth setup and many community hosting threads (VPS/Docker/security advisories)

Cron doc deep read: jobs can load skills, run in a --workdir (injects AGENTS.md, isolates per task identity), gateway ticks every 60s with file lock, jobs.json plus execution ledger with scheduled instant, external worker per job, explicit note that this is not exactly-once for side effects

Persistent Memory doc: bounded MEMORY.md (2,200 chars) and USER.md (1,375 chars) injected as a frozen snapshot at session start, add/replace/remove only, injection/exfiltration scanning of entries, optional write_approval gate, one agent per Hermes home warning, SQLite FTS5 session_search as unbounded recall, external memory providers
Skills doc: skill_manage create/patch/delete/write_file as the agent's procedural memory, advisory linter, create-after-complex-task triggers, skills vs memory split
Hermes Desktop feature list (queueing, per-session YOLO toggle, context meter, comment mode annotate, preview rail, model picker scoped to chat) read before planning the web UI
First request_user_input scoping question (audience: personal desktop vs hosted multi-user vs small team) and the follow-up web research opening desktop, bot-mode, api-server and bot-screen docs

API Server and Programmatic Integration docs: runs API with SSE events (tool.started/completed, subagent.*), idempotency keys, stop/steer/approval endpoints, MCP trust-gate consent surfacing as approval.request, jobs CRUD API, sessions REST API with fork, /v1/skills and /v1/toolsets discovery, per-profile run scoping, detached delegation completions never start unsolicited turns

Remaining Desktop doc: Settings->Gateways multi-connection registry (local, remote URL, Hermes Cloud) and desktop launches hermes serve over tui_gateway JSON-RPC; Bot Screen threat model details (RFB socket, DevTools port, single-use display_ticket)

SpaceXAI 'Designing Grok Bot' article: Bots (not chats) as primary objects with roster/presence, avatar-as-state (idle/thinking/working/waiting/blocked/done), hover for current action, computer as the bot's workspace with status/preview/takeover levels, inline cards/widgets in a heterogeneous transcript, tools and skills account-level while memory and routines are per-bot, coordinator bots instead of dashboards, routines triggered by schedule or events (GitHub/Linear/Slack/webhook), caps of ~50 bots per account and 6 per group

Grok Bot docs 'Use the computer and apps': shared per-account cloud computer with one screen per bot (shared cookies/files/CLI credentials, screens not security boundaries), human takeover for passwords/2FA/CAPTCHA/payment, secure secret request masked from the conversation, connectors installed as account-wide plugins from a Marketplace and preferred over clicking

Re-opened Bot Mode and Bot Screen pages (duplicate of earlier reads) plus Docker setup doc: hermes-agent image, s6-overlay per-profile gateway supervision, volume at /opt/data, resource minimums, API_SERVER_PORT per profile, docker as terminal backend vs running Hermes in Docker, Chromium baked in
Docker doc find-passes (compose file, 8642 gateway API port, 9119 dashboard, resource limits, audio passthrough, local inference servers) and Bot Screen sandbox image notes

Second and third request_user_input rounds: Hermbot scoping decisions captured as user answers (private workspace, web first then desktop later, all functions able to collaborate manually or autonomously like Grok Bot; local POC then server; review external writes; Google/Slack/GitHub connectors)

Search for groups/peers/hosted-room-authority and bot-mode docs; Sessions doc: session key formats per platform, group_sessions_per_user isolation default, no daily reset, SQLite state.db with FTS5; toolsets reference (core/composite/platform toolsets, MCP server toolsets, kanban opt-in)

Deployment/action-policy question results (local POC then server, review external writes, Google+Slack+GitHub) and developer-guide research on adding tools, plugin system (ctx.register_tool/hook/command, plugin.yaml, capabilities consent), plugin LLM access, toolsets reference
API Server Jobs API and sessions API recap plus Slash Commands, Web Search provider plugins, local_knowledge plugin catalog entries read to learn extension points

Fourth request_user_input round: workspace visibility (private plus shared; user said private first for POC), UI fidelity (close to Grok Bot UX with Hermbot branding), model access (owner-managed providers)

Grok Bot docs 'Message and collaborate': composer features (/ skills, @ mentions of bots/groups/routines/connectors, reply/react, steer in-progress work, editable drafts before email/Slack send), direct message priority and 'Stop now', groups of 2-6 with single-owner handoffs, threads vs reactions, search palette, keyboard shortcuts, async bot-to-bot handoff wakes receiver

Grok Bot docs 'Settings and notifications' (attention states: needs attention vs unread vs working; per-bot notification toggle, suppression when focused, auto-review rules where Ask-first wins, local-egress routing) and 'Team Bots' (shared team bot with team memory, private per-person chats, acts as the asking person, plugin credential modes)

Hermes Event Hooks doc fetch, environment probe (docker present, node missing, python3 present) and Bot Mode/API Server re-reads for peer DM, hosted room authority transfer (groups.promote/demote with fencing) and sessions REST
Fifth request_user_input round: bot management scope when one bot manages others (answer: tasks and lifecycle, configuration changes via user approval)

Read local openai-docs skill file and searched OpenAI docs on Codex plan mode/goal/side chats/ExecPlans/PLANS.md/Implement.md/Documentation.md: patterns for long-horizon agent work (plan then goal, side chats, milestone verification, status docs) that shaped the planning process and plan/README structure rather than the product itself

Codex slash-commands and desktop keyboard-shortcut references (/plan, /goal, /side, /compact, /fork, attention shortcuts, approve/decline shortcuts); evidence for command-palette and attention-needed UX conventions

Final searches on how to turn off Codex plan mode (slash commands, changelog, config reference), ending in the last request_user_input asking whether to save the approved plan to plan/README.md and start Phase 1

decisions.decision: A bot is a thin layer over a runtime profile (own config, memory, skills, credentials, chat history) rather than a new primitive
decisions.why: Hermes Bot Mode explicitly models a Bot as a profile so everything is also visible from the CLI and nothing new needs to be learned
decisions.alternatives: Dedicated bot object with its own store
decisions.tradeoffs: Ties bot identity to the runtime's profile layout

decisions.decision: Per-bot model/provider pin, SOUL, per-skill/toolset/MCP enablement and copy-of-credentials at creation; single-use OAuth logins are not copied
decisions.why: Specialists should get only the capabilities they need and credentials must not be shared across OAuth single-use grants
decisions.alternatives: Inherit everything from a default profile

decisions.decision: Cap roughly 50 bots per account and 6 per group; limit concurrently warm local bot backends
decisions.why: Grok Bot removed controls and set practical limits; Hermes keeps at most N warm bot backends and waits 30s for a slot
decisions.tradeoffs: Requires slot handling and queue timeouts

decisions.decision: Bot management by another bot limited to tasks and lifecycle proposals, with configuration changes requiring user approval
decisions.why: User answered the scoping question choosing tasks and lifecycle (not full admin, not orchestration only)
decisions.alternatives: Task orchestration only; full approved administration

decisions.decision: One permanent canonical Bot Chat per bot; /new compacts rather than forks; archiving retires and starts a fresh canonical chat
decisions.why: Bot Mode treats the bot relationship as a forever-chat; Grok article argues disposable chats do not fit an agent that remembers

decisions.decision: Composer features borrowed from Grok Bot: / for saved skills, @ for bots/groups/routines/connectors, reply/thread/react, steering while work runs, editable drafts before send, Stop now
decisions.why: User chose close UX fidelity to Grok Bot with Hermbot branding

decisions.decision: Heterogeneous transcript where conversation, system events, interactive cards and visualizations share one timeline
decisions.why: Grok found prose-only answers forced users to restructure results

decisions.decision: Direct user messages take priority over background work and can redirect the current turn; queue vs steer is a deliberate choice
decisions.why: Grok docs state direct messages redirect work; OpenAI notes accidental mid-turn steering costs more than waiting

decisions.decision: Idempotency-keyed run creation for retry-safe intake over the runtime API
decisions.why: Hermes runs API reserves keys durably so identical retries return the original run

decisions.decision: Treat the form of an answer as part of the answer: inline cards for drafts, routines created, settings changed, bot-to-bot messages
decisions.why: Grok Bot moved from narrated prose to structured widgets

decisions.decision: Plan then goal: plans answer how, goals answer what must be true before done; durable goals persist across turns
decisions.why: OpenAI Codex long-horizon guidance on /plan vs /goal

decisions.decision: Group rooms of 2 to 6 bots with bounded serial rounds (3) and message caps (10), @mention scoping, bots may pass, @user escalation raising needs-you
decisions.why: Hermes Bot Mode caps keep rooms from spinning; Grok caps six per group

decisions.decision: Bot-to-bot handoff via asynchronous message_agent with attribution, delivery ids, typed failure reasons and at-most-one retry for transient errors
decisions.why: Hermes Bot Mode design; Grok bots wake and reply later
decisions.tradeoffs: Fire-and-forget needs polling or notification for replies

decisions.decision: Coordinator bots (chief of staff) handle routine routing instead of dashboards, assignment boards or handoff controls
decisions.why: Grok found those added coordination work for the user

decisions.decision: Room authority and ordering belong to a single durable driver with lease; failover is an operator procedure that fences the old writer
decisions.why: Hermes documents divergent histories if two writers accept messages

decisions.decision: Each member keeps a hidden per-room session whose context carries messages since its last turn up to about 200 messages or 32k chars
decisions.why: Bounds prompt growth; oversized members need compression

decisions.decision: Background run model: runs with SSE events, stop, steer, approval endpoints; detached completions never start unsolicited model turns
decisions.why: Hermes runs API semantics the Hermbot runtime adapter was designed against

decisions.decision: Cron-style execution is not an exactly-once side-effect guarantee
decisions.why: Hermes ledger records scheduled instant and attempts but admits interrupted runs may repeat

decisions.decision: Avatar carries lifecycle state (idle/thinking/working/waiting/blocked/done) with hover for current action instead of step logs
decisions.why: Users asked for detail mainly for reassurance that the bot was working
decisions.alternatives: Animated dots or written current step

decisions.decision: Sidebar distinguishes needs-attention (question/approval/handoff) from unread activity from working
decisions.why: Grok settings docs define these states; Hermes adds needs-you badge on groups

decisions.decision: Artifacts are durable outputs bots create or modify (documents, designs, code, data) as a first-class concept alongside bots, chats, prompts and tools
decisions.why: Grok conceptual model of five concepts

decisions.decision: Right-hand preview rail and in-app browser comment/annotate mode with selectors and computed styles for feedback on artifacts
decisions.why: Hermes Desktop features

decisions.decision: Bounded curated memory (MEMORY.md/USER.md) frozen at session start plus unbounded FTS5 session search and optional external providers
decisions.why: Hermes memory design keeps prompt cost fixed while recall is on demand
decisions.tradeoffs: Cannot see mid-session saves until next session

decisions.decision: Memory entries scanned for injection/exfiltration patterns and optionally gated by write_approval
decisions.why: Memory is injected into the system prompt so it is an injection vector

decisions.decision: Per-bot memory and per-role context, with shared context only via group chats
decisions.why: Grok: merging legal and finance histories into one memory degrades relevance

decisions.decision: Do not point two agent processes at the same Hermes home
decisions.why: Memory writes race and reload into prompts
decisions.tradeoffs: One runtime process per bot home

decisions.decision: Tools and skills live at account level while memory and routines belong to the bot
decisions.why: Grok capability vs context boundary

decisions.decision: Custom tools should be plugins (tools, hooks, slash commands, capability-gated overrides), not core patches; skills preferred when instructions plus shell suffice
decisions.why: Hermes developer guide

decisions.decision: Toolsets as named bundles (core, composite, platform, per-MCP-server) with opt-in workflow-gated toolsets
decisions.why: Hermes toolsets reference

decisions.decision: MCP write-capable tools on untrusted servers require approval consent
decisions.why: Hermes API server surfaces trust-gate as approval.request

decisions.decision: Each bot has its own screen with status, preview and takeover levels; human takes control for login/2FA/CAPTCHA/payment then hands back
decisions.why: Grok and Hermes Bot Screen both follow this pattern; the computer is the workspace not a supervision surface

decisions.decision: Screens are work surfaces, not security boundaries; bots share the OS user, files and browser
decisions.why: Documented threat model in both products
decisions.tradeoffs: Do not store credentials one bot must not use

decisions.decision: computer_use approval maps to runtime modes (standard, bounded with reviewed manifest, unrestricted); destructive actions refused when no one can answer and hard-blocked combos exist
decisions.why: Hermes safety design
decisions.tradeoffs: Cron computer use needs a reviewed manifest

decisions.decision: Browser work goes through the browser toolset not computer_use; browser sessions persist across handoff
decisions.why: Hermes docs

decisions.decision: Prefer a structured connector over clicking a website; connectors are installed account-wide via a marketplace of plugins
decisions.why: Grok docs

decisions.decision: Milestone connectors chosen by the user: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Slack, GitHub plus extensible MCP and browser access
decisions.why: User answered the connected-apps question

decisions.decision: Team bots act as the asking person for OAuth plugins and use the bot's own credential for key-based plugins
decisions.why: Grok Team Bots credential modes
decisions.alternatives: Lend one person's login to all

decisions.decision: Routines are standing responsibilities attached to a bot, triggered by schedule or events (issues, PRs, webhooks, Slack, Linear), shown in the bot's main interface
decisions.why: Grok moved routines from secondary config into the main interface

decisions.decision: Routines implemented as namespaced cron jobs [bot:<name>] whose runs land in the bot's chat history
decisions.why: Hermes Bot Mode

decisions.decision: Scheduler ticks every 60s with a file lock; jobs may load skills and run in a workdir
decisions.why: Hermes cron design

decisions.decision: Events (webhooks, GitHub PRs/issues, Slack messages, workflow failures) start sessions just like prompts or other bots
decisions.why: Grok article notes sessions can start from a schedule, event or another bot

decisions.decision: Room log records turn.started/turn.settled and streams member activity to plugins via on_room_member_activity hook
decisions.why: Hermes hooks for observability

decisions.decision: Roster with avatar, last message, unread, hide, sections and pin; hiding is display-only
decisions.why: Bot Mode roster behavior

decisions.decision: Per-session YOLO toggle, context-usage meter, cache hit rate in status bar
decisions.why: Hermes Desktop

decisions.decision: Per-bot notification setting; OS/mobile notifications when a bot finishes or needs input, suppressed while the app is focused; hidden bots never toast but badge a dot
decisions.why: Grok settings and Hermes hidden-bot behavior

decisions.decision: Errors appear above the composer as dismissible notices with request ids; clearing does not undo external actions
decisions.why: Grok settings docs

decisions.decision: Private workspace with accounts and invited teammates, no public signup or billing; owner-managed provider credentials
decisions.why: User answers: private workspace, owner-managed providers

decisions.decision: Private bots/DMs first, with explicit sharing of bots and groups later
decisions.why: User noted POC is private first

decisions.decision: Team Bot chats stay private per teammate; owner cannot read teammates' chats
decisions.why: Grok Team Bots
decisions.tradeoffs: Team memory is the only shared surface

decisions.decision: Wrap the Hermes runtime through its API server (runs, sessions, jobs, skills/toolsets discovery) bearer-gated by API_SERVER_KEY with per-profile scoping
decisions.why: Documented programmatic surface
decisions.tradeoffs: Runtime upgrades change surface; capabilities endpoint helps detection

decisions.decision: Profiles are not a sandbox; real isolation requires container/terminal backends
decisions.why: Hermes profile docs explicit

decisions.decision: Bot Mode protocol injection requires exact title 'Bot Chat' plus a ui_meta hermes-bots marker, so headless installs must write both
decisions.why: Documented conditions in Bot Mode

decisions.decision: Run Hermes in Docker (nousresearch/hermes-agent) with data volume, s6 supervision per profile and moderate resource limits (1-4GB, 1-2 CPU); Chromium is the heaviest
decisions.why: Docker setup docs

decisions.decision: Local POC first then always-on Linux server; Docker locally
decisions.why: User deployment answer

decisions.decision: Hosted cloud variant scales to zero with per-second compute and separate inference billing
decisions.why: Hermes Cloud pricing page

decisions.decision: Verification at every milestone with lint, typecheck, tests and build; plan file as source of truth plus status/decisions doc
decisions.why: OpenAI long-horizon Codex runbook pattern

decisions.decision: Doctor-style triage command for environment checks (computer-use doctor with exit codes)
decisions.why: Hermes computer-use doctor
